title: A Staged Story Brings Absalom Home
overview: Joab uses a made-up court case to persuade King David to bring back his exiled son Absalom, who killed his brother, but the return is cold and halfway until Absalom forces a meeting.

parts.label: Joab's plan (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Absalom had killed his half-brother Amnon for raping their sister Tamar and fled abroad to Geshur, and Joab, David's army commander, sees that David is torn about him. The Hebrew of verse 1 can mean David's heart longed for Absalom or was set against him, so scholars are unsure, but either way Joab hires a clever woman to act out a grieving widow.

parts.label: The widow's invented case (vv. 4-11)
parts.note: She claims one of her sons killed the other, and the family now wants the survivor executed, which would also leave them his inheritance. In that culture a close relative, called the avenger of blood, had the duty to kill a killer, and her line about her last burning coal means her final hope of keeping her husband's family line alive, so David swears to protect the son.

parts.label: Turning it on David (vv. 12-17)
parts.note: Now she points out that David has just spared someone else's son who killed a brother, yet keeps his own son, who also matters to the whole nation, in exile. Her saying that life is like spilled water and that God finds ways to bring the banished back is a plea to show mercy before it is too late, and Christians have sometimes heard in it a picture of God's reconciling work in Jesus.

parts.label: David sees through it (vv. 18-24)
parts.note: David guesses Joab is behind the act, and she admits it while flattering him as wise as an angel. He agrees to bring Absalom back but refuses to see him, so the son is home in Jerusalem but shut out from his father.

parts.label: Absalom's looks and family (vv. 25-27)
parts.note: The writer pauses to describe Absalom as the most admired man in Israel, famous for his heavy hair, which he cut and weighed once a year. The exact modern weight is uncertain, and naming his daughter Tamar likely honors the sister whose rape started this whole tragedy.

parts.label: A burned field and a kiss (vv. 28-33)
parts.note: After two years of being ignored, Absalom gets Joab's attention by setting his barley field on fire and demands to see the king, even if it means death. David finally receives him with a kiss, but nothing is said about apology or real healing, and the next chapter shows Absalom plotting against his father.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether David's recall of Absalom was true mercy or a father's weakness that set aside justice for a killer and helped lead to the rebellion that followed.
think: When a relationship is badly broken, what is the difference between letting someone back in and actually being reconciled?
